title: PSG Preprocessing Pipeline
text: typical workflow four steps: Sleep-EDF file uses linked-ear channel names (EEG Fpz-Cz, EEG Pz-Oz). already matched prepare_psg()’s default EEG pattern, recording uses notation like C3-A2 can pass rename map preprocessing step: preprocess_psg() following order, full continuous signal re-epoching (avoids filter discontinuities epoch boundaries):
code: library(mrpheus)  # 1. Read EDF rec <- read_edf("SC4001E0-PSG.edf")  # 2. Epoch and classify channels psg <- prepare_psg(rec) psg$channel_map # 3. Preprocess: rename, remove DC, notch, bandpass psg_clean <- preprocess_psg(   psg,   channel_rename = c(     "C3-A2" = "C3", "C4-A1" = "C4",     "O1-A2" = "O1", "O2-A1" = "O2"   ) ) # 4. Automatic AASM sleep staging on the cleaned PSG stages <- stage_epochs(psg_clean) head(stages)

code: # Standard EEG passband eeg_bp <- bandpass_filter(eeg, sr = sr, low_hz = 0.3, high_hz = 35)  # High-pass only (baseline drift removal) — set high_hz beyond Nyquist eeg_hp <- bandpass_filter(eeg, sr = sr, low_hz = 0.1, high_hz = Inf)  # Low-pass only — set low_hz to 0 eeg_lp <- bandpass_filter(eeg, sr = sr, low_hz = 0, high_hz = 35)

title: PSG Preprocessing Pipeline
text: notch bandpass filters use zero-phase IIR (Butterworth) designs applied via gsignal::filtfilt(): Notch: 2nd-order Butterworth bandstop (≈9 coefficients). Safe long recordings — memory issues. Bandpass: 4th-order Butterworth. high_hz cutoff automatically clamped 99 % Nyquist frequency prevent instability. Zero-phase (filtfilt) filtering introduces phase distortion doubles effective filter order. prefer causal (single-pass) filter reason, use gsignal::filter() directly Butterworth coefficients. staging pipeline (stage_epochs()) applies separate MNE-matched FIR bandpass internally — preprocess_psg() filtering staging filtering independent.

title: PSG Preprocessing Pipeline
text: Ocular artefacts (blinks, saccades, slow drift) contaminate EEG channels volume conduction eyes. mrpheus provides two correction methods, operating continuous signal returning new mrpheus_psg cleaned epochs.

title: PSG Preprocessing Pipeline
text: correct_eog_regression() regresses EEG channel EOG reference channels replaces EEG residuals. removes transient blinks slow ocular drift without requiring blink event detection. recommended method : one two EOG channels want fast, deterministic result. recording relatively EEG channels (fewer 4). Slow drift contamination concern alongside blinks. can restrict channels used:
code: psg_eog <- correct_eog_regression(psg_clean) psg_eog <- correct_eog_regression(   psg_clean,   eog_channels = c("EOG LOC", "EOG ROC"),   eeg_channels = c("EEG C3", "EEG C4", "EEG O1", "EEG O2") )

title: PSG Preprocessing Pipeline
text: correct_eog_ica() decomposes EEG independent components via FastICA, identifies whose time courses correlate EOG channels threshold, subtracts contribution. Key parameters: ICA requires least 2 EEG channels. recordings fewer 3–4 EEG channels, regression reliable. threshold controls sensitivity: lower values flag components (aggressive removal, risk removing genuine signal); higher values conservative.
code: psg_eog <- correct_eog_ica(psg_clean) psg_eog <- correct_eog_ica(   psg_clean,   n_components = 6L,    # default: min(6, n_eeg_channels)   threshold    = 0.35   # default: Pearson |r| above which a component is flagged )

title: PSG Preprocessing Pipeline
text: standard overnight PSG 4+ EEG channels, ICA generally produces cleaner results. 2-channel ambulatory recording, use regression.
